request.system: You are an expert in clinical classification systems.

messages.content:
ICD-10-AM is the Australian modification of the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, 10th revision. Its disease codes are arranged in chapters, and a three-character category is written as one capital letter followed by two digits. The letter indicates the chapter or block: A and B are infectious diseases, C is malignant neoplasms, D is other neoplasms and blood disorders, E is endocrine, nutritional and metabolic disease, F is mental and behavioural disorders, G is the nervous system, H is the eye and ear, I is the circulatory system, J is the respiratory system, K is the digestive system, L is the skin, M is the musculoskeletal system, N is the genitourinary system, O is pregnancy and childbirth, P is the perinatal period, Q is congenital malformations, R is symptoms and abnormal findings, S and T are injury and poisoning, and Z is factors influencing health status. The two digits narrow the chapter to a specific category, for example J44 is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and N17 is acute kidney failure.

The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Using that structure, assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. Choose the chapter letter first, then the two digits.

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient Name: [redacted]
Medical Record Number: [redacted]
Date of Admission: [redacted]
Date of Discharge: [redacted]

Hospital Course:
The patient was admitted to our hospital with shortness of breath, dry coughing and fever, after testing positive for COVID-19. The patient was intubated and put on ventilator support within 36 hours of presentation, as he had severe hypoxia and increased work of breathing. Treatment was initiated with various medications to manage his COVID-19 symptoms. 
Throughout his 31-day hospital course, the patient's clinical condition was complicated by septic shock, acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), volume overload, and uncontrolled diabetes. The chest X-ray revealed bilateral pneumothoraces, which were confirmed with a chest CT, along with pneumomediastinum. The patient was transferred to a hospital where thoracic surgery was available. Imaging after transfer showed that the pneumothorax had slightly increased without tension physiology. The PEEP was decreased from 8 to 6 cm H20 where it remained till his discharge. On the 31st day of admission the patient passed away from hypoxic respiratory failure.
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Procedures:
The patient was intubated and put on ventilator support within 36 hours of presentation. 

Hospital Course:
The patient was admitted with COVID-19 and developed severe hypoxia and increased work of breathing. Treatment was initiated with various medications to manage his COVID-19 symptoms. Throughout his hospital course, the patient's clinical condition was complicated by septic shock, ARDS, volume overload, and uncontrolled diabetes. The patient passed away from hypoxic respiratory failure on hospital day 31.

Outcome:
The patient passed away from hypoxic respiratory failure after a prolonged hospital stay. 

Follow-Up:
N/A

Discharge Medications:
N/A 

Follow-up Instructions:
N/A

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
In ICD-10-AM, COVID-19 is coded U07.1 (virus identified) and U07.2 (clinically diagnosed). The question asks for a three-character category, and the stated chapter letters do not include U. Even so, U07 is the correct category for COVID-19 as the principal diagnosis in ICD-10-AM.

The prompt's list of chapters does not mention U, but the instruction is to assign the correct code. The patient was admitted with confirmed COVID-19 pneumonia-type illness, and the condition chiefly responsible for the admission was COVID-19. The ARDS, respiratory failure and septic shock are complications. In ICD-10-AM, COVID-19 with a positive test is U07.1, so the category is U07.

Alternatively, J12 (viral pneumonia) could apply if pneumonia were documented, but the record does not state it. The category U07 is therefore the best fit.

CODE: U07
